overview: Hoover forwards a 1941 memo on two Japanese ships at Manzanillo, Mexico, carrying military personnel, sealed diplomatic baggage, strategic goods, and repatriating Japanese residents amid special Mexican courtesies.

subfiles.title: Hoover letter to Berle enclosing memorandum on Japanese ships at Manzanillo
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Hoover forwards a confidential memorandum concerning recent Japanese shipping activity at Manzanillo, Mexico.
subfiles.summary: Hoover sends Berle a confidential memo on Japanese ships at Manzanillo, also shared with other intelligence agencies.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the Heiyo Maru and Noto Maru at Manzanillo
subfiles.from: Federal Bureau of Investigation, based on a confidential source
subfiles.about: The memorandum reports the movements, passengers, mail, baggage, cargo, and official treatment of two Japanese merchant ships calling at Manzanillo in September 1941.
subfiles.summary: Memo details two Japanese ships at Manzanillo carrying military officers, sealed diplomatic boxes, strategic goods, and over 100 repatriating passengers, amid alleged special Mexican courtesies.

interest: Shows 1941 FBI intelligence on Japanese ships in Mexico carrying diplomats, cargo, and possibly war materials.
